device.description: 12-bit 40 kSPS low-power sampling ADC with internal reference and serial interface
device.note: ads8512.pdf (SLAS485) p.3-4 specifications (conversion time 20 us, VIH, binary two's complement, VS 4.75-5.25 V, bus access/relinquish 83 ns), p.5 pin configuration and terminal functions, p.12 Table 2 conversion and data timing, p.13 Table 3 output codes, p.14-15 internal/external DATACLK (12-bit format, MSB first)

pages: p.3-4 (conversion time 20 us max, VIH 2.0 V to VS+0.3 V, binary two's complement, VS 4.75-5.25 V, bus access 83 ns, relinquish 83 ns), p.5 (pin configuration and terminal functions), p.12 (Table 2: t9 conversion 12 us typ / 15 us max, t20 DATA valid 20 ns max), p.13 (Table 3: 0 V = 000h), p.14-15 (12-bit, MSB first; external DATACLK: transmission begins on the first rising edge, data valid on the falling edge)
notModeled: analog inputs, input-range resistor network (R1IN/R2IN/R3IN/BUF wiring, Table 1), internal 2.5 V reference (REF), reference buffer output BUF and CAP compensation node; codeFormat is binary two's complement on every range (0 V reads 0000h on the bipolar ranges; on the unipolar ranges 0 V is -full scale, which the model does not give)

only the external data clock mode (EXT/INT high) is modeled: SPI mode 1 framed by CS falling; the first DATACLK rising edge starts the transmission with the MSB, each bit valid on the falling edge (Figures 40-41). The internal-clock mode (EXT/INT low: the part drives DATACLK during conversion n+1 with the result of conversion n, Figure 39) is not modeled; DATACLK is never driven

a CONV falling edge starts a conversion regardless of CS and is ignored while one runs; the shift register is updated just before BUSY rises and the result is lost if DATACLK is high with CS low then (t25, Figure 37/38) - not modeled
CS high 3-states BUSY as well as DATA (and DATACLK); the model drives BUSY regardless of CS

tValid/tFloat use the bus access / relinquish times (83 ns max, specifications table); t26/t27 give only 15 ns minimums. Conversion time uses the specifications table's 20 us maximum (Table 2 t9 gives 15 us max).
PWRD (power-down, conversions invalid while low power) is not read; CONV pulse/quiet-time rules (t2-t5), throughput limits
